gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 18?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Ensemble forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and German Weather Service (DWD) cluster Munich’s August 18 maximum near 19–21 °C. Strengthening westerly flow advects cooler maritime air, while persistent cloud cover and scattered showers reduce solar insolation and suppress daytime heating below the late-August climatological average of 22–23 °C. Operational guidance from AccuWeather and similar models aligns with a 19–20 °C high under mostly cloudy skies and possible morning showers. With leading market probabilities tightly grouped around these values, traders are reflecting model consensus on the precise timing and coverage of cloud breaks versus precipitation, which will determine whether the daily maximum settles at 18 °C, 19 °C, or 20 °C. Final official observations from DWD stations will resolve the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service short-range guidance and ensemble model consensus position New York City’s August 17 high near 80–81°F under light southerly flow, moderate humidity, and partly cloudy skies typical of mid-August climatology. Official observations from stations such as LaGuardia and Central Park, combined with real-time surface data, reinforce this narrow range and have driven overwhelming trader consensus toward the 80-81°F bin. This market-implied probability reflects skin-in-the-game assessment of current atmospheric conditions rather than a guarantee. A rapid increase in insolation from unexpected clearing or stronger warm-air advection could push readings into the low 80s, though such shifts appear unlikely given the stabilizing synoptic pattern and proximity to daily maximum.

Trader consensus, reflected in the 42.5% implied probability on 31°C, accounts for typical model spread and historical August variability around the 31°C climatological average, with lower odds on 33°C+ underscoring uncertainty in short-term convective development ahead of final observations.

Urban heat island effects from concrete surfaces further elevate readings, yet increased cloud cover and any scattered showers could cap peaks near 31–32°C. Trader consensus, reflected in the 42.5% implied probability on 31°C, accounts for typical model spread and historical August variability around the 31°C climatological average, with lower odds on 33°C+ underscoring uncertainty in short-term convective development ahead of final observations.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from the ECMWF and German Weather Service cluster Munich’s August 18 maximum near 19–21 °C under strengthening westerly flow, persistent cloud cover, and scattered showers that suppress daytime solar heating relative to the seasonal 22–23 °C climatology. These conditions create the narrow spread of market-implied odds among 20–22 °C bins, as modest differences in cloud timing or shower intensity can shift the observed peak by 1–2 °C. Official resolution will depend on the highest 2-meter temperature recorded by DWD stations, with limited upside risk if breaks in cloud cover occur earlier than modeled.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the German Weather Service (DWD), Met Office, and BBC indicate a ridge of high pressure over central Europe will support daytime maxima in Munich of 28–30°C on August 19, positioning 29°C as the market leader at 48.5% implied probability. This setup favors the upper end of the seasonal distribution, as late-August climatological averages hover near 22–25°C. Model consensus across European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and national agencies clusters tightly around 27–29°C, though minor differences in timing of peak heating and local effects introduce uncertainty between 28°C and 30°C outcomes. Updated short-range guidance released in the past 24–48 hours has reinforced these values ahead of the final observation window.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and AccuWeather guidance for New York City on August 18 points to mostly sunny conditions under a strengthening high-pressure ridge, with light northwest winds and typical late-summer humidity supporting a daily maximum near 84–86°F. This aligns with the market’s heaviest weighting on the 84–85°F bin, as model consensus and Central Park climatology (average August high of 83°F) favor a modest above-normal outcome without triggering stronger heat advection or convective cooling. Official observations through early afternoon and short-range ensemble runs show limited spread, reducing odds of excursions above 87°F or below 83°F. Traders appear to be pricing the latest forecast updates and the narrow remaining window for significant deviation before evening.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 Aug '26.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts and real-time observations position Tokyo’s August 18 maximum temperature at 31°C, driving the 99.5% market-implied probability. Ensemble model consensus, historical August baselines around 31°C, and current atmospheric conditions—including moderate humidity, light winds, and limited solar heating—support this outcome while keeping deviation risks low. A shift to 32°C or higher would require stronger high-pressure ridging or unexpected clear-sky intensification, scenarios with minimal support in the latest guidance. Traders’ capital-weighted consensus reflects confidence in these verified measurements over broader seasonal averages.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts for Tokyo on August 20 indicate mostly cloudy skies with a chance of showers and maximum temperatures near 32°C, aligning with the market's clustered probabilities around 30–32°C. Primary drivers include the strength of the Pacific High, which supports above-normal summer heat, tempered by variable cloud cover that limits solar heating and any afternoon precipitation timing that could suppress peaks. Ensemble model spreads highlight uncertainty in exact maximums due to urban heat island effects and humidity levels typical for late August, where small shifts in steering patterns or insolation can differentiate outcomes between 30°C and 33°C. eventMetadata.context_description: Current ensemble guidance from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and German Weather Service (DWD) clusters Munich’s maximum temperature near 19–21 °C on August 18, reflecting strengthening westerly flow that advects cooler maritime air, combined with persistent cloud cover and scattered showers that reduce solar insolation and enhance evaporative cooling. These conditions suppress typical late-summer surface heating and keep the daily high well below August climatological norms of 22–23 °C. Operational forecasts from AccuWeather and others align on a 19–20 °C peak under mostly cloudy skies with morning showers, driving the market’s tight clustering on 19–21 °C outcomes. Minor model spread in shower timing, cloud thickness, and boundary-layer mixing accounts for the close probabilities between 20 °C and 22 °C, with any unexpected clearing or delayed precipitation offering the main upside risk for a higher reading.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official short-range forecasts from the DWD, Met Office, and BBC converge on a daytime high of 28–30 °C for Munich on August 19, directly explaining why those three bins capture over 80 % of market-implied probability. Model consensus reflects building high pressure, light westerly flow, and mostly sunny intervals that allow modest daytime warming above the seasonal August average of roughly 23 °C. Low precipitation risk and limited cloud cover further support the central range, while the narrow spread of outcomes reflects typical late-summer variability rather than extreme heat or cooling advection. Updated model runs released on August 18 have reinforced this narrow band, leaving little room for the tails priced below 1 %.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent JMA and ensemble forecasts position Tokyo’s August 20 maximum near 31–32 °C under mostly cloudy conditions with light showers possible, producing the tight clustering of market-implied odds around those values. Persistent summer humidity and the urban heat island effect support readings at or above the 31 °C climatological average, while increased cloud cover and modest precipitation reduce peak solar insolation enough to keep the outcome below 33 °C in most model runs. Small differences in timing of any showers or afternoon clearing, plus minor variations across official measurement sites, explain the spread among the 30–32 °C brackets; traders are weighting the consensus guidance that has held steady over the past 48 hours.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecast guidance from the ECMWF and DWD places Munich’s August 18 maximum near 19–21 °C, reflecting trader consensus on those tightly bunched outcomes. Strengthening westerly flow, persistent cloud cover, and scattered showers are limiting daytime solar heating and suppressing late-summer warmth that would otherwise push readings higher. Official resolution hinges on the Munich Airport station measurement, with model runs continuing to converge on this narrow band rather than the seasonal average near 22–23 °C. Minor shifts in cloud timing or shower intensity could still nudge the final high between 19 °C and 21 °C before evening.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Tokyo's highest temperature on August 19, 2026, centers on 31–32°C as the dominant range (combined ~72% implied probability), reflecting short-term forecast consensus and seasonal atmospheric patterns.** 

Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) guidance and ensemble models indicate a daytime high near 32–33°C under the influence of a strong subtropical Pacific High, which promotes subsidence, clear skies, and enhanced solar heating typical of mid-August. This setup, combined with elevated sea-surface temperatures around Japan and the urban heat island effect in Tokyo, favors readings in the low 30s rather than extremes. 

Recent JMA seasonal outlooks have consistently projected above-normal temperatures for summer 2026, driven by the Pacific High’s persistence after an early rainy-season end, sustaining the heat pattern observed through mid-August. Short-range updates for August 19 specifically align with historical climatology (normal high ~31°C) but tilt slightly warmer, narrowing the distribution around 31–32°C while keeping lower probabilities on 30°C or 33°C+ outcomes. 

Model agreement and the absence of disruptive fronts or typhoon influences in the immediate forecast window reinforce this positioning, though small shifts in steering flow or cloud cover could adjust the peak by 1°C on the day.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Tokyo's highest temperature on August 19, 2026, centers on 31–32°C as the dominant range (combined ~72% implied probability), reflecting short-term forecast consensus and seasonal atmospheric patterns.** 

Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) guidance and ensemble models indicate a daytime high near 32–33°C under the influence of a strong subtropical Pacific High, which promotes subsidence, clear skies, and enhanced solar heating typical of mid-August. This setup, combined with elevated sea-surface temperatures around Japan and the urban heat island effect in Tokyo, favors readings in the low 30s rather than extremes. 

Recent JMA seasonal outlooks have consistently projected above-normal temperatures for summer 2026, driven by the Pacific High’s persistence after an early rainy-season end, sustaining the heat pattern observed through mid-August. Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) guidance and ensemble models indicate a daytime high near 32–33°C under the influence of a strong subtropical Pacific High, which promotes subsidence, clear skies, and enhanced solar heating typical of mid-August. This setup, combined with elevated sea-surface temperatures around Japan and the urban heat island effect in Tokyo, favors readings in the low 30s rather than extremes. 

Recent JMA seasonal outlooks have consistently projected above-normal temperatures for summer 2026, driven by the Pacific High’s persistence after an early rainy-season end, sustaining the heat pattern observed through mid-August. Short-range updates for August 19 specifically align with historical climatology (normal high ~31°C) but tilt slightly warmer, narrowing the distribution around 31–32°C while keeping lower probabilities on 30°C or 33°C+ outcomes. 

Model agreement and the absence of disruptive fronts or typhoon influences in the immediate forecast window reinforce this positioning, though small shifts in steering flow or cloud cover could adjust the peak by 1°C on the day.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 19 Aug '26.

Market-implied odds therefore cluster on 31–32°C as traders weigh these verified guidance products against historical precedent, with resolution hinging on the official daily maximum recorded at the Tokyo station.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts and ensemble model consensus position Tokyo’s August 20 maximum near 31–32°C, aligning with the market’s heavy weighting on those outcomes. Mid-August climatology shows a long-term average high of about 31°C, but increased cloud cover and scattered showers expected tomorrow are limiting solar heating and capping potential extremes below 32°C. High humidity typical of the season enhances perceived heat yet rarely drives record daily maxima without clear skies or stronger southerly flow. Updated model runs and any shifts in precipitation probability over the next 24–48 hours will likely refine trader sentiment ahead of resolution.
